title: Leaving a vague promise behind

captions.energy: Ending an unsuitable form of answer

meaning: You can thoughtfully leave an unsuitable form of promise behind and feel free to discuss wishes anew without presenting them as a settled plan.
text: On Vishuddha, the way you promise matters alongside the answer itself. The Hermit in the physical position helps you explain what reflection has made clear about your own words. Death in energy supports willingness to end a form of answer that no longer conveys genuine agreement. The Fool in emotions brings lightness and a sense of beginning afresh. Released from an old formula, conversation can become curious again even when you do not yet know what follows.

For example, a discussion of a weekend together brings up the familiar “You will see, I will think of something”. You explain that these words create an expectation of a surprise, although no specific idea exists yet. **Leaving a vague promise releases a living idea**. You leave the phrase behind and start exchanging possibilities without turning the first appealing one into an agreement. You can laugh at an unexpected suggestion and enjoy the conversation’s freshness without committing to arrange that particular day.

A difficult moment appears if the new lightness is taken as proof that earlier expectations have all disappeared. Thoughtfully ending the formula then sounds like trying to forget what it already promised. The constructive purpose of ending helps name the boundary of the change: which form you are leaving now, and what still needs an answer. A new beginning can remain free while respecting words already spoken.
